examples.text: From the pitch of Cape-Fraward, to the pitch of Cape-Holland, the Streight lies in the Channel West and by North, nearest, and is distant full five Leagues;

examples.text:

examples.text: Alba the emperor was crook-backed, Epictetus lame; that great Alexander a little man of stature, Augustus Cæsar of the same pitch […].

examples.text: Laban with his brethren pitched in the Mount of Gilead.

glosses: To move so that the front of an aircraft or boat goes alternatively up and down.

examples.text: The airplane pitched.

glosses: To set at an angle, especially a downwards one; to cause to tilt.

examples.text: Driveway cross slopes along Owyhee Street in Boise reach nearly 9%, which could cause a person in a wheelchair or using another mobility device to be pitched into the street. The cross slope should be no greater than 2% in order to prevent this.

examples.text: The only way to get on the green from here is to pitch the ball over the bunker.

glosses: To bounce on the playing surface.

examples.text: The ball pitched well short of the batsman.

glosses: To settle and build up, without melting.
To alight; to settle; to come to rest from flight.

glosses: To fix one's choice.

examples.text: […]pitch the road with hard stones [rather] than to break them up for a road covering

glosses: To set or fix (a price or value).

examples.text:

glosses: To discard (a card) for some gain.

glosses: Mover la cabeza, inclinándola con frecuencia adelante, atrás o a los lados.

Inclinarse a una parte más que a otra una cosa que balancea y que debe estar en equilibrio.
